```{r setup}
library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr)
library(forcats); library(ggplot2); library(scales); library(knitr)

# --- Validated colour palette (dataviz reference palette; CVD-checked) --------
C_BLUE   <- "#1c5cab"   # primary magnitude
C_BLUE_L <- "#86b6ef"   # light companion (planned / part-of-whole)
INK  <- "#11161c"; INK2 <- "#52514e"; MUTED <- "#8a8a86"
GRID <- "#e7e7e3"; SURFACE <- "#ffffff"

theme_report <- function(base = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base) +
  theme(
    plot.background   = element_rect(fill = SURFACE, colour = NA),
    panel.background  = element_rect(fill = SURFACE, colour = NA),
    panel.grid.minor  = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    axis.ticks = element_blank(),
    axis.title = element_blank(),
    axis.text.y = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(colour = INK2, size = base - 1),
    plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = base + 3, colour = INK,
                                 margin = margin(b = 2)),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = base - 1, colour = INK2, margin = margin(b = 14)),
    plot.caption  = element_text(size = base - 4, colour = MUTED, hjust = 0,
                                 margin = margin(t = 12)),
    plot.title.position = "plot", plot.caption.position = "plot",
    legend.position = "top", legend.justification = "left",
    legend.title = element_blank(), legend.text = element_text(colour = INK2),
    legend.margin = margin(b = 2),
    plot.margin = margin(16, 20, 12, 14))
}
lab <- function(mapping) geom_text(mapping, colour = INK, fontface = "bold",
                                   size = 3.4, vjust = -0.5)

fisc  <- read_csv("data_clean/fiscal_outturn.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
cats  <- read_csv("data_clean/findings_by_category_tidy.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
paras <- read_csv("data_clean/unresolved_paragraphs.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
obs   <- read_csv("data_clean/notable_observations.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(headline_amount = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(headline_amount)))
contr <- read_csv("data_clean/contracts_flagged.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(across(c(contract_value, amount_at_issue), ~suppressWarnings(as.numeric(.))))

money <- function(v, cur) {
  ifelse(is.na(v), "not stated",
  ifelse(cur == "USD",
    ifelse(v >= 1e6, paste0("US$", comma(v/1e6, accuracy = 0.1), "m"),
                     paste0("US$", comma(v, accuracy = 1))),
    ifelse(v >= 1e9, paste0("K", comma(v/1e9, accuracy = 0.01), "bn"),
    ifelse(v >= 1e6, paste0("K", comma(v/1e6, accuracy = 0.1), "m"),
                     paste0("K", comma(v, accuracy = 1))))))
}
short_min <- function(x) x |>
  str_replace("Ministry of ", "") |>
  str_replace("Office of the President - Provincial Administration", "Provincial offices") |>
  str_replace("Office of the Vice President \\(DMMU\\)", "Disaster unit (DMMU)")
```

> **What this is.** Every year, Zambia's Auditor General checks how the government collected and spent public money, and publishes a report. This page sums up five of those reports, for the years 2021 to 2025, in plain language. Every figure comes straight from the reports, and the page number is on record.
>
> **One thing to keep in mind.** An audit "finding" is a question the auditors could not close, not a proven crime. It means the records did not fully add up, or an explanation was still owed when the report was written. So read these as "money the government could not fully account for," not "money that was stolen."

# The short version

```{r headline}
f <- fisc |> filter(financial_year == 2025)
tibble(
  " " = c("Government planned to spend (2025)","Government actually spent (2025)",
          "Left unspent against the plan (2025)","Surplus: collected minus spent (2025)",
          "Open audit questions in 2025","Open audit questions in 2022"),
  "Amount / figure" = c(
    money(f$final_budget_payments, "ZMW"), money(f$actual_payments, "ZMW"),
    money(f$final_budget_payments - f$actual_payments, "ZMW"),
    money(f$surplus_deficit, "ZMW"), "27", "40")) |> kable()
```

Over these five years:

- The government is spending a **bigger share of its budget** than before: 76 out of every 100 Kwacha budgeted in 2022, rising to about 86 in 2025.
- Its **surplus has shrunk**, from about K30 billion in 2022 to about K2 billion in 2025. It now collects and spends much closer to the line.
- The **number of unresolved audit questions has fallen**, from 40 in 2022 to 27 in 2025.
- But the **same ministries keep coming up** year after year, and the reports still list large sums not collected, not delivered, or not properly supported, including specific contracts (below).

# How government money moved

Each report compares what the government **planned** to spend (the final budget) with what it **actually** spent.

```{r budget-chart}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.6
fisc |> filter(!is.na(actual_payments)) |>
  select(financial_year, Planned = final_budget_payments, Spent = actual_payments) |>
  pivot_longer(-financial_year, names_to = "which", values_to = "k") |>
  mutate(which = factor(which, levels = c("Planned","Spent"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(financial_year), k/1e9, fill = which)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .72), width = .64) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(k/1e9, accuracy = 1), group = which),
            position = position_dodge(width = .72), vjust = -0.5,
            colour = INK, size = 3.3, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Planned = C_BLUE_L, Spent = C_BLUE)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .12))) +
  labs(title = "What government planned to spend vs what it spent",
       subtitle = "Kwacha, billions",
       caption = "Source: Office of the Auditor General, Statement B (budget execution), page 5 of each report. 2021 not reported.") +
  theme_report()
```

In 2025 the government planned to spend about **K251 billion** and spent about **K216 billion**. The roughly **K34 billion** gap is money budgeted but not spent in the year. Under-spending is not automatically good or bad: it can mean restraint, but also projects running late or funding that did not arrive.

A **surplus** means the government collected more than it spent that year. That surplus has been getting smaller.

```{r surplus-chart}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
fisc |> filter(!is.na(surplus_deficit)) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(financial_year), surplus_deficit/1e9)) +
  geom_col(fill = C_BLUE, width = .62) +
  lab(aes(label = comma(surplus_deficit/1e9, accuracy = 0.1))) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .14))) +
  labs(title = "Surplus: money collected minus money spent",
       subtitle = "Kwacha, billions",
       caption = "Source: Office of the Auditor General, Statement B, page 5 of each report.") +
  theme_report()
```

*(The 2021 report does not include this budget table, so 2021 is left out of this section.)*

# What the auditors flagged, and how much

When the auditors cannot fully account for money, they record it under a category, such as money not collected, irregular payments, or funds not properly supported by documents. The 2022 and 2023 reports add these into a single table, the only two years with a comparable total.

```{r findings-chart}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.6
pick <- tibble(financial_year = c(2021L,2022L,2023L), report_year = c(2022L,2023L,2023L))
series <- cats |> inner_join(pick, by = c("financial_year","report_year")) |>
  mutate(arrears = str_detect(str_to_lower(category_printed), "tax arrears"))
series |> group_by(financial_year) |>
  summarise(`All findings` = sum(amount_kwacha, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Without the tax-arrears line` = sum(amount_kwacha[!arrears], na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(-financial_year, names_to = "measure", values_to = "k") |>
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = c("All findings","Without the tax-arrears line"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(factor(financial_year), k/1e9, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .72), width = .64) +
  geom_text(aes(label = comma(k/1e9, accuracy = .1), group = measure),
            position = position_dodge(width = .72), vjust = -0.5,
            colour = INK, size = 3.1, fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("All findings" = C_BLUE,
                               "Without the tax-arrears line" = C_BLUE_L)) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .12))) +
  labs(title = "Value of audit findings each year",
       subtitle = "Kwacha, billions",
       caption = "Source: Office of the Auditor General trend tables, 2022 and 2023 reports, page ii.") +
  theme_report()
```

One line dwarfs the rest: **unpaid tax arrears**, which the tax authority (ZRA) reports separately and which runs into tens of billions of Kwacha. It is a running backlog of taxes owed, not money that went missing in the year. Set it aside (the lighter bars) and the rest of the findings are far smaller, and do not simply fall every year.

# Real examples: what was not collected, not delivered, or not supported

Specific cases the reports single out. Amounts are exactly as the reports state them. Kwacha (K) and US dollar (US$) items are kept separate.

**Money the government was owed but did not collect:**

```{r cases-revenue}
obs |> filter(section == "Revenue", !is.na(headline_amount)) |>
  arrange(desc(financial_year), desc(headline_amount)) |>
  transmute(Year = financial_year, Ministry = short_min(ministry_std),
            `What the report records` = observation,
            Amount = money(headline_amount, currency), Page = paste0("p", source_pdf_page)) |>
  kable()
```

**Money spent, at risk, or not delivered:**

```{r cases-expenditure}
obs |> filter(section == "Expenditure", !is.na(headline_amount)) |>
  arrange(desc(financial_year), desc(headline_amount)) |>
  transmute(Year = financial_year, Ministry = short_min(ministry_std),
            `What the report records` = observation,
            Amount = money(headline_amount, currency), Page = paste0("p", source_pdf_page)) |>
  kable()
```

# Contracts the auditors questioned

This is a first set of named contracts the reports flag, with who got the contract, its value, whether it was delivered, and what the auditors questioned. It is drawn from the reports' highlighted cases; the full bodies name many more, which is the next piece of work.

```{r contracts-summary}
n <- nrow(contr)
undel <- sum(contr$delivered %in% c("No","Partial"))
ss <- sum(str_detect(contr$procurement_method, "single-source|uncompetitive"))
flagprice <- sum(str_detect(contr$issue_flagged, "overpriced|unsupported|price not established|under-declaration"))
```

Of the **`r n`** contracts highlighted here, **`r undel`** were not fully delivered or were terminated, **`r ss`** used single-source or uncompetitive procurement, and several were flagged for overpricing, unsupported fees, or under-declared value.

```{r contracts-table}
contr |>
  arrange(desc(financial_year)) |>
  transmute(Year = financial_year,
            Ministry = short_min(ministry_std),
            Supplier = supplier,
            `Contract` = description,
            Value = money(contract_value, contract_currency),
            Delivered = recode(delivered, "NA" = "not stated", .missing = "not stated"),
            `Auditors flagged` = issue_flagged,
            Page = paste0("p", source_pdf_page)) |>
  kable()
```

Read these the same way as the rest: a flagged contract is a question the auditors raised, not a proven loss. "Delivered: No" means the records did not show delivery when the report was written.

# Which ministries come up most often

The reports are organised by ministry. Counting how often each appears with an unresolved question shows who recurs, even where no single total is given.

```{r recurrence-chart}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
paras |> group_by(ministry_std) |>
  summarise(years = n_distinct(financial_year), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(years == 5) |>
  mutate(name = short_min(ministry_std), name = fct_reorder(name, n)) |>
  ggplot(aes(n, name)) +
  geom_col(fill = C_BLUE, width = .72) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.4, colour = INK, fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, .1))) +
  labs(title = "Ministries flagged in every report, 2021 to 2025",
       subtitle = "Number of unresolved-finding sections over the five years",
       caption = "Source: Office of the Auditor General, contents pages. A count of sections, not an amount of money.") +
  theme_report() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(colour = INK2, size = 11),
        axis.text.x = element_blank())
```

Nine portfolios appear in **every** report over the five years. Provincial offices under the Office of the President come up most, then Finance, Agriculture, Home Affairs, Education, and Health. This shows where problems recur, not which ministry lost the most money.

# How to read these numbers fairly

- **A finding is a question, not a verdict.** Say "the report records K3.56 billion in unpaid obligations," not "the ministry lost K3.56 billion."
- **Not every year lines up.** The budget table is missing for 2021; the single findings total exists only for 2022 and 2023; the 2024 and 2025 reports list examples instead of one total.
- **One huge line (tax arrears) distorts the totals**, so it is shown separately.
- **US dollar and Kwacha amounts are never added together.**
- **The contracts list is a first set**, drawn from highlighted cases, not every contract in the reports.
- These figures come from the published main reports only. Ministries may have since given explanations, recorded in later reports and parliamentary committees.

# Where this comes from

Five reports from the Office of the Auditor General of Zambia, *Reports on the Accounts of the Republic*, for the years ended 31 December 2021 to 2025. Cite any figure with the report year and the page shown here, for example *Auditor General, 2025 report, page 5.*

The full data, the page reference for every number, and the code behind each chart are in the project repository: **https://github.com/Chanza-bj/AG_Report_Analysis**
